Interpreting the FOMC statement through standard monetary-policy lenses still yields a mildly positive but cautious tone: solid growth, strong labor market, below-2% inflation, and gradual rate hikes with continued balance-sheet normalization. Incorporating the November 2017 Beige Book nudges the tone modestly more positive than a SLOOS-only read: districts reported continued expansion from October to mid-November; consumer spending was supported in retail and autos with an upbeat holiday-sales outlook; labor markets were tight with notable wage gains in professional, technical, and production roles; and hurricane rebuilding increased demand and construction-material costs—pointing to firmer wage/cost pressures. These Beige Book signals partially offset the October SLOOS’s mixed-to-soft credit conditions (tightening in key consumer segments and weaker loan demand), though they don’t eliminate the caution from sub-2% inflation and credit headwinds. Net effect: slightly stronger than previously assessed, but still cautious.
